findings.asked: Car and trailer: equations of motion, tension, then the car's new acceleration after the tow-bar breaks.
findings.wentWrong: Many could not write an equation for the trailer alone and tried the whole system or the car; arithmetic slips followed; the post-break acceleration was widely unattempted.
findings.rule: Write F = ma for each body separately; after a break, recompute the resultant force on what remains.

findings.asked: Two blocks over a pulley: diagram, equations, force on the pulley, later motion.
findings.wentWrong: Tension arrows wrong; g omitted; equations of motion poorly formed and badly solved simultaneously; many did not know the force on the pulley was double the tension here; the earlier acceleration (or +10) was reused after the string went slack.
findings.rule: Force on a pulley = resultant of the two tensions (2T when the strings hang parallel); a free particle then moves under gravity alone.

findings.asked: Connected blocks: diagram, then equations for each.
findings.wentWrong: Normal reaction missing on one block; different labels for the same tension; weight labelled M; arrows missing; F = ma attempted where it was not needed; equations like T - 90 = Ma were produced by many.
findings.rule: One string, one T; write each block's equation in its own direction of motion.

findings.asked: Car towing: resistive force, 'show that' a mass, then motion after separation.
findings.wentWrong: Substituting the later value of M into part (i) got zero; verifying by substitution got at most two marks; some used the car's motion for the trailer part; follow-through was given for a correct negative acceleration.
findings.rule: Derive, do not verify; after separation each body has its own resultant force.

findings.asked: Two blocks and a pulley: diagram, acceleration, tension, force on the pulley.
findings.wentWrong: Treating the masses separately worked better than the whole system; T - 30 - 80 = 8a mixed weights and masses; the force on the pulley was assumed to be 2T when the string geometry made it a different resultant - the least well answered item on the paper.
findings.fullMarkAnswersDid: Found T, then added the two tension vectors along the string directions to get the magnitude of the force on the pulley.
findings.rule: The pulley feels the vector sum of the two tensions; 2T only if the string sections are parallel.

ruleToRemember: Write F = ma for each particle in its direction of motion with the same T and a; the force on the pulley is the resultant of the two tensions (2T only when the strings are parallel); after a string breaks or a tow-bar snaps, recalculate the acceleration from the forces that remain.
aStarSignal: Computing the force on a pulley whose strings are not parallel, and handling the motion after a connection breaks.
